chunk_findings.detail: The test now feeds `[test] argv = "acme -p hi"` and expects `h.reserved["test"].values == {"argv": "acme -p hi"}`. An `argv` value is an argument vector, so the wire shape should be a TOML array (`argv = ["acme", "-p", "hi"]`), not a single string. With the current string, any consumer that treats `argv` as an argument vector will pass the whole `"acme -p hi"` as one executable/argument instead of program `acme` with arguments `-p hi`, so the descriptor is malformed; the test asserts the malformed raw value and therefore no longer checks a valid wire-shape row.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_descriptor_v2.py:80

chunk_findings.detail: `--json` install/uninstall always emit `written: false` for both a dry-run that still needs a write and a true no-op, and exit 0 either way. `ddflow --json completion install` without `--yes` when the block is absent returns `{written: false, path, message: "would append..."}`; the same fields (only the prose differs) come back for `--yes` when the file is already installed. A client that trusts the structured body and treats `written: false` as "nothing to do" never re-runs with `--yes`, so the completion block is never installed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/parsers/completion.py:_say

chunk_findings.detail: The same prompt now requires two incompatible MCP calls. The intro still says `ddflow_perf action=report`, while the "exact next call" example was changed to `ddflow_perf format=<fmt> window=<win>` with no action, and the alias sentence says the report is "also reachable as `ddflow_perf`" with no arguments. An agent that copies the example omits `action=report`; one that follows the intro sends it. One of those calls does not match the tool.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/commands/perf_report.md:3
